title: More efficient engines made Britain burn more coal, not less
body: In 1865 economist William Stanley Jevons pointed out that Britain’s coal use had soared after James Watt’s far more efficient steam engine arrived. Because each unit of work became cheaper, steam power spread into many more industries and total consumption rose. Economists now call this a rebound effect. Its size varies a lot and efficiency usually does save resources, but the Jevons paradox shows that saving is not guaranteed.

slides.clue: Economists’ name for efficiency savings being eaten up by extra use: the ___ effect
slides.detail: When the rebound passes 100%, so that efficiency raises total use, it is the Jevons paradox. Usually it stays below that.
